Text Embeddings · Text Embeddings02

Training a BPE Tokenizer

Broadly speaking, we can train our tokenizer by repeatedly looking for common pairings of tokens and merging them to create a new token.

[21, 9, 6, 0, 4, 2, 21, 0, 20, 2, 21, 0, 16, 15, 0, 21, 9, 6, 0, 14, 2, 21, 0, 2, 15, 5, 0, 2, 21, 6, 1]

[2, 21]: 4 [21, 9]: 2 [9, 6]: 2 [4, 28]: 1 [20, 28]: 1 [16, 15]: 1 [14, 28]: 1 [2, 15]: 1 [15, 5]: 1 [28, 6]: 1

[21, 9, 6, 0, 4, 28, 0, 20, 28, 0, 16, 15, 0, 21, 9, 6, 0, 14, 28, 0, 2, 15, 5, 0, 28, 6, 1]

An untrained tokenizer is effectively just a character-level tokenizer.

Embeddings

Text Embeddings · Text Embeddings08

Text Embeddings

Converting tokens to embeddings allows us to interpret them as points in high dimensional space, which then allows us to compare them against each other!

Text Embeddings · Text Embeddings09

Text Embeddings

One way to think about it, is that each axis encodes some artifact of language, plurality, color, gender…

How similar they are on a given axis measures how similar they are on that "thing".

NOTE: Technically the similarity is often on a higher-dimensional manifold than a singular axis, but it's a good way to think about it

Text Embeddings · Text Embeddings10

Axes in the Brain

Mitchell et al. (Science, 2008) scanned 9 people with fMRI while they looked at 60 nouns (celery is one).

  • Each noun got 25 axes: how often it appears near 25 verbs (eat, taste, push, ride, …) in a trillion-word text corpus. Celery's eat value: 0.84.
  • A linear model from those 25 numbers to brain activity, fit on 58 nouns, told the 2 left-out nouns apart 77% of the time (chance is 50%).

Huth et al. (Nature, 2016): 7 people, over 2 hours of The Moth Radio Hour, every word described by its co-occurrence with 985 common words. The result is a map of meaning across both sides of the cortex, broadly similar from person to person.

Embeddings built from co-occurrence can predict brain activity. They don't show the brain learns meaning by counting.

Text Embeddings · Text Embeddings11

Measuring Text Embedding Similarity

Instead of using euclidean distance, we often measure the similarity of text embeddings using cosine similarity, which measures the angle between two vectors. This is because we often care about direction, rather than magnitude.

Text Embeddings · Text Embeddings18

Programming Day 04: Text Embeddings

Today we write irishQwen's EmbeddingLayer (irishQwen/embedding.py):

  • __init__: a weight matrix W of shape (embed_dim, vocab_size), one column per token
  • forward: look up the columns for a batch of token ids, (B, T) → (B, T, C)
  • backward: add the gradient into the columns of the tokens that were used
  • update: one step of gradient descent

import torch
import math
class EmbeddingLayer():
def __init__(self, vocab_size, embed_dim):
self.W = torch.randn(embed_dim, vocab_size) \
* math.sqrt(2.0 / vocab_size)
self.dW = torch.zeros_like(self.W)
def forward(self, tokens):
self.tokens = tokens
E = self.W[:, tokens] # (C, B, T)
E = E.permute(1, 2, 0) # (B, T, C)
return E.contiguous()
torch.manual_seed(0)
layer = EmbeddingLayer(512, 256)
tokens = torch.tensor([[446, 309, 44, 32,
275, 327, 294, 309]])
out = layer.forward(tokens)
print(tokens.shape, "->", out.shape)
print(torch.equal(out[0, 1], out[0, 7])) # " be" twice
Output
torch.Size([1, 8]) -> torch.Size([1, 8, 256])
tensor(True)

Indexing W[:, tokens] is the same as T @ E without building T.

import torch.nn.functional as F
def backward(self, dY):
C, V = self.W.shape
flat = self.tokens.reshape(-1) # (B*T,)
dY_flat = dY.reshape(-1, C) # (B*T, C)
T = F.one_hot(flat, V).float() # (B*T, V)
self.dW = dY_flat.T @ T # (C, V)
def update(self, lr):
self.W -= lr * self.dW
EmbeddingLayer.backward = backward
EmbeddingLayer.update = update
layer.backward(torch.ones(1, 8, 256))
used = (layer.dW[0] != 0).nonzero().reshape(-1)
print(used)
print(layer.dW[0, 309], layer.dW[0, 446])
Output
torch.Size([1, 8]) -> torch.Size([1, 8, 256])
tensor(True)
tensor([ 32,  44, 275, 294, 309, 327, 446])
tensor(2.) tensor(1.)

Only the columns of tokens in the batch get a gradient, and " be" (309), used twice, gets twice as much.
